scope: MEASUREMENT ONLY -- the reinforce default and the ranking are unchanged by this probe

prior_art.cold_stream: README (1.15.0 correction) and CHANGELOG already publish reinforcement as a confound depressing recall on a COLD query stream (~0.10 at low k). The cold arm here is a control reproducing that sign, not a new result.
prior_art.determinism: tests/test_recall_is_deterministic.py already establishes run-to-run determinism and that reinforcement was not its cause.
prior_art.insert_order: core.py ~5584 newest-first tie-break is deliberate policy (`tie_recent`), so insert-order sensitivity is by design.

primary_warm_heldout.design: train on a Zipf query stream (reinforce=True vs reinforce=False vs a gold-only ORACLE bump), then evaluate HELD-OUT questions with reinforce=False on all three arms, so the arms differ only in the state training left behind

transfer_coverage.meaning: fraction of HELD-OUT questions whose gold record was also the answer to some TRAINING question. This is the ceiling on what any popularity prior could buy: for the remaining questions no prior about the right record can exist at evaluation time, so training can only add noise.

oracle_hit1.note: upper bound: value bumped ONLY on the record that was right. Not a proposal and not in the library -- it separates 'the prior is harmful' from 'the prior is estimated from what was returned rather than what was correct'.

b_insert_order_BY_DESIGN.property: insert-order sensitivity (same records, different write order)
b_insert_order_BY_DESIGN.by_design: core.py ~5584 tie-breaks on (-score, -insertion_position): newest-first. This is the documented policy `tie_recent` builds on, not a defect, and it is NOT part of the read-purity total.

c_query_order_reinforce_true.property: read-purity (same store, different QUERY order), reinforce=True

c_query_order_reinforce_false.property: read-purity (same store, different QUERY order), reinforce=False

d_admit_write_path.property: write-path read-purity: admit() calls recall(t, k=1) (core.py ~7002; remember_dedup() the same at ~2561). Read `divergence_excess_over_time_control`, NOT `divergence`: an untouched store moves on elapsed time alone, and the raw figure is mostly that.
d_admit_write_path.control: a time-matched twin store, built beside the treated one and read interleaved with it, is never handed to admit(). Whatever it moves is the clock; only the excess over it is evidence about the write path, and only when every trial agrees on the sign

divergence_decomposition.note: the 2026-07-28 '49-90% of answers change on reorder' figure, apportioned. Arm (b) is policy, not a defect; the read-purity number is arm (c) with reinforce=True.
